title: Remark
body_md: Before turning to the proof of this proposition, we would like to point out two facts about the force coefficients $\upomega^n_{\varepsilon,\mu}$. Firstly, we control them in a topology where the weight in space is absent. In other words, the complications due to the growth of the stochastic terms in large volume that we had to tackle for the fractional Laplacian are not present here. Secondly, the right-hand side of (\@saveref{eq:boundomega}) shows that these coefficients are built from the stationary force coefficients $\upxi^{2,0;n}_{\varepsilon,\mu}$ pathwise, which is an interesting feature of our construction. In particular, with a little more effort, we can prove that they are continuous in the stationary force so that convergence of the stationary force implies convergence of these force coefficients.

label: Prop:HermiteSpacesInterpolation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Prop:HermiteSpacesInterpolation}
    Let $1<p<\infty$, $1\leqslant q<\infty$ and $\eta\in{{\mathchoice{\hbox{\bfR}}{\hbox{\bfR}} 
        {\hbox{\scriptsize\bfR}}{\hbox{\tiny\bfR}}}}$. Then, the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \par\hangindent 40\p@ For any $\eta_0\neq\eta_1\in{{\mathchoice{\hbox{\bfR}}{\hbox{\bfR}} 
        {\hbox{\scriptsize\bfR}}{\hbox{\tiny\bfR}}}}$ and $0<\theta<1$, such that $\eta=(1-\theta)\eta_0+\theta\eta_1$,
        $$\mathscr{H}^{\eta,p} = \left[\mathscr{H}^{\eta_0,p},\mathscr{H}^{\eta_1,p}\right]\egroup\egroup\egroup\egroup_\theta\,,$$
        with equivalent norms.
        \par\hangindent 40\p@ For any $1<p_0\neq p_1<\infty$ and $0<\theta<1$, such that $\frac{1}{p}=\frac{1-\theta}{p_0}+\frac{\theta}{p_1}$,
        $$\mathscr{H}^{\eta,p} = \left[\mathscr{H}^{\eta,p_0},\mathscr{H}^{\eta,p_1}\right]\egroup\egroup\egroup\egroup_\theta\,,$$
        with equivalent norms.
        \par\hangindent 40\p@ If $0<\eta<1$,
        $$\mathscr{B}^{\eta}_{p,q} = \bgroup\bgroup\bgroup\bgroup\left(L^p_x,\mathscr{H}^{1,p}\right)\egroup\egroup\egroup\egroup_{\eta,q}= \bgroup\bgroup\bgroup\bgroup\left(L^p_x,\mathscr{H}^{2,p}\right)\egroup\egroup\egroup\egroup_{\frac{\eta}{2},q}\,,$$
        with equivalent norms.
        \par\hangindent 40\p@ If $\eta<0$, for any $\eta_0\neq\eta_1<0$ and $0<\theta<1$, such that $\eta=(1-\theta)\eta_0+\theta\eta_1$,
        $$\mathscr{B}^{\eta}_{p,q} = \bgroup\bgroup\bgroup\bgroup\left(\mathscr{H}^{\eta_0,p},\mathscr{H}^{\eta_1,p}\right)\egroup\egroup\egroup\egroup_{\theta,q}\,,$$
        with equivalent norms.
    \end{enumerate}
